# SQL source syntax and scanner qualification

The baseline is the published `tree-sitter-sequel` 0.3.11 archive, SHA-256
`9d198ad3c319c02e43c21efa1ec796b837afcb96ffaef1a40c1978fbdcec7d17`.
Its VCS metadata names `7b51ecda191d36b92f5a90a8d1bc3faef1c7b8b8` with a dirty
checkout. The published grammar, build script and highlight query match that
commit. The omitted MIT license is restored verbatim from the same commit.
Tree-sitter CLI 0.24.7 with ABI 14 reproduced the published parser, grammar JSON
and node types byte for byte before local syntax changes. The exact published
grammar and six generated source files remain alongside the active inputs with
an `.orig` suffix; their independent hashes are recorded in `grammars.lock`.

The preferred grammar adds typed, written T-SQL procedure headers, physical
parameters and scalar/table declarations, bracket-delimited raw identifiers,
MAX type arguments and IDENTITY column clauses. Procedure bodies admit a
bounded supported statement grammar: explicit BEGIN/END blocks or one unbraced
statement. GO is not whitespace, and unsupported control flow remains a parse
gap. This slice does not establish complete T-SQL syntax or catalog semantics.
Bracket syntax must preserve the existing PostgreSQL array and dollar-function
contracts. Ambiguous implicit bracket aliases do not establish a dialect-specific
interpretation. Malformed headers, missing delimiters and recovered procedure errors
cannot establish valid declaration owners in the structural adapter.

The active static tables are regenerated from the reviewed preferred grammar
using the pinned local Tree-sitter CLI 0.24.4, Node.js 24.11.1 and ABI 14. Two
independent preparations must produce identical generated bytes. Cargo consumes
only those checked-in native inputs; it neither invokes the generator nor
fetches sources. This preparation does not reproduce the original upstream
tables and does not prove an independently network-blocked, empty-cache build.

The scanner retains complete UTF-8 dollar delimiters in fixed-capacity state.
Snapshots have a version byte, a little-endian two-byte length and the exact
delimiter bytes. Empty state has zero serialized bytes. Only complete tags
that fit the existing 1024-byte native ABI frame can enter persistent state;
oversized tokens fail without mutating prior context. Malformed frames reset
the state instead of retaining a partial tag or an unchecked C string.

Serialization does not consume live context. Deserialization and scanning do
not allocate per delimiter; allocation failure at construction fails closed.
Literal scanning preserves overlapping dollar prefixes, embedded NUL body
bytes and case-sensitive Unicode delimiters. It leaves the enclosing function
delimiter intact when scanning a differently tagged literal.

The grammar's permissive punctuation tags are preserved. This scanner bounds
source tokens, not SQL dialect validity or database name resolution. The native
state and syntax regression suites live in `tests/native-grammars`; SQL text is
never executed by these tests. This package alone is not a structural adapter
or evidence of complete SQL semantic coverage.
